title: Find if Array Can Be Sorted
summary: Given a 0-indexed array of positive integers nums, determine if the array can be sorted in ascending order by performing any number of operations.
statement: Given a 0-indexed array of positive integers nums, determine if the array can be sorted in ascending order by performing any number of operations. An operation consists of swapping any two adjacent elements that have the same number of set bits in their binary representation. Return true if the array can be sorted in this manner, otherwise return false.
constraints: nums is a nonempty array of positive integers.
Only adjacent values with equal set-bit counts may be swapped.
Return whether repeated legal swaps can put nums in nondecreasing order.
hints: Legal swaps permute values only within each maximal contiguous block of one popcount.
For every block, compare its minimum with the maximum of all preceding blocks.
Scan blocks, track min/max, reject when previous_max>block_min, then update previous_max.
Each block can be internally sorted arbitrarily, but blocks cannot cross; the boundary inequality is therefore necessary and sufficient for their sorted concatenation.
editorial: Each block can be internally sorted arbitrarily, but blocks cannot cross; the boundary inequality is therefore necessary and sufficient for their sorted concatenation.

tests.explanation: The one-bit block can become 2,4,8 and the four-bit block can become 15,30, yielding sorted order.
The leading two-bit value three cannot cross the following one-bit block, so sorting is impossible.
